proposal.diagnostic_alternative: A flat result could reflect assignment switching in steps 51-75 or late overwriting rather than amplitude, in which case interval2 at tick 1 is weak transmission instead of a monotone lever and the +2 asymmetry would have to be explained by correspondence churn rather than by delivered displacement.

If that effect is a property of the late window rather than of the interval2=5 background, the same two-tick raise at the new anchor will lower condition mean by roughly 6e-4 A while costing roughly 6e-5-1e-4 pic50 of teacher agreement, leaving Best essentially flat.
